chapter: New York, church bands and early training
title: The Clef Club and the Amsterdam Club
summary: Briggs explains the Clef Club and Amsterdam Club as booking offices where musicians waited for society gigs, and the Clef's building on 52nd Street.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay, tell me about that. The Clef Club was really very important in those days --
Very, very important. The Clef Club was more or less like -- the Amsterdam as well, but on a lesser scale -- they were more like booking offices.
Yes.
You see, musicians would go to the Clef Club and become members and almost live in the club. You know --
They had a building?
They had a building, yes. It was 52nd Street, almost touching the El.
The Sixth Avenue El?
Yes, the Sixth Avenue El. On 52nd Street.
52nd Street?
Uh, huh. And, the musicians they would go
Briggs
to the Clef Club around about mid-day, and stay all day until a gig comes in or if it doesn't come in, no matter what, a gig or anything else, you see.
Right.
And the work that they had, it was more or less a type of society work. I don't mean society music. Playing for what you call the "smart set".
Right.
People who had, you know— And they had all that tied up. If they had too much work then they would turn some of the work over to the Amsterdam.
Well, the Amsterdam was what, that was a black club as well?
A black club as well, yes. A black club -- the Amsterdam was a black club of lesser importance.
For fellows who couldn't get into the Clef they would get into
Briggs
the Amsterdam.
Oh you would get into the Amsterdam before you would --
Work your way up to the Clef?
Yeh.
Now as I understand it, and you can correct me obviously, if I'm wrong here.--
Yes.
As I understand it, up until around that time, the black musicians had most of the work sewed up and then the white players came in later; is that right?
Yes, I think you're right, because -- yes, I think you're right. It seems just what I said about the Clef Club, they had so much work, they'd turn it over to the Amsterdam.
